title: Choose LumenLink's visual world
question: Keep the optical bench, take a challenger, or ask for a fresh roll.

options.label: Optical Bench
options.lineage: camera calibration cards and hands-on optics exhibits
options.thesis: Privacy becomes a visible beam passing directly from screen to camera.
options.viewport: A screen and camera face each other across a calibrated light corridor; Send and Receive are the two physical endpoints.
options.risk: Can feel clinical unless the controls stay tactile and the copy stays human.
options.case: Best on both axes: familiar physical cues for everyday users and a literal proof of the product mechanism.

options.label: First Light
options.lineage: theater cyclorama lighting from blackout to day
options.thesis: A file crosses the app as a cue of light that grows from darkness into arrival.
options.viewport: Two devices sit on opposite sides of a horizon; the transfer beam raises the scene from blackout to day.
options.risk: The atmosphere can outrun the plain send-or-receive decision.
options.case: Stronger emotional identification, weaker product clarity than Optical Bench.

options.label: Direct Broadcast
options.thesis: Every workflow is a numbered local broadcast page with nothing behind the screen.
options.viewport: Page 100 makes Send and Receive large numbered destinations inside an exact character grid.
options.risk: Feels technical and nostalgic to users who never lived with teletext.
options.case: Very clear navigation, but weaker everyday identification and a less literal privacy proof.

options.label: Private Tension
options.lineage: tensegrity sculpture in carbon rod and red cord
options.thesis: The local link holds because every device and state is visibly connected.
options.viewport: Send and Receive become two anchored nodes joined by a live red transfer path with states pinned to its joints.
options.risk: The force metaphor needs explanation before it reads as optical transfer.
options.case: Fuses poorly: its counterforce story obscures the simple one-way handoff.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A restrained product dashboard with clear actions and conventional trust cues.
canonCard.viewport: A centered promise, two familiar action cards, and a concise local-only proof row.
canonCard.risk: Highly usable, but visually interchangeable with other privacy software.
